tasks.title: Create KV cache wrapper with soft lock
tasks.objective: Create worker/src/cache/kvCache.ts implementing get<T>, set<T>, and getOrFetch<T> operations against Cloudflare KV, replacing the in-memory CacheManager. Include best-effort soft lock for request coalescing.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: get<T>(kv, key) returns parsed JSON value or null when key is missing
set<T>(kv, key, value, ttlSeconds) writes JSON string to KV with expirationTtl
getOrFetch returns cached value on hit without calling fetcher
getOrFetch calls fetcher on cache miss and writes result to KV
getOrFetch writes a fetching:{key} soft lock marker with 30s TTL before calling fetcher

tasks.technical_notes: The KV mock should implement { get(key): Promise<string|null>, put(key, value, opts): Promise<void>, delete(key): Promise<void> }. The soft lock pattern: on cache miss, check if fetching:{key} exists -> if yes, wait 500ms and retry get once -> if still null, proceed to fetch. The lock marker uses 30s TTL so it auto-expires. This is best-effort, not guaranteed single-flight.

embedded_context.constraints: ADR-001: KV has eventual consistency (reads may be stale for up to 60s). Best-effort coalescing is acceptable (NG-008). Free tier: < 1000 KV writes/day target, so set operations must use expirationTtl in seconds (not ms). Note: KV TTL is in seconds, existing CacheManager uses milliseconds -- conversion needed.

tasks.title: Implement cron handler entry point with scheduled dispatch
tasks.objective: Implement worker/src/index.ts with the scheduled event handler that dispatches to weather, tide, and water quality refresh functions based on event.cron. Tide refresh must skip null tideStationId beaches and deduplicate by station ID.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: When event.cron matches '*/30 * * * *', the handler refreshes weather for all 9 beaches
When event.cron matches '0 * * * *', the handler refreshes tides for unique non-null stations only (1 station currently)
When event.cron matches '0 */6 * * *', the handler refreshes water quality for all 9 beaches
Tide refresh skips beaches where tideStationId is null (Trout Lake)
If one beach refresh fails, the handler continues processing remaining beaches and does not throw

tasks.technical_notes: The handler inspects event.cron to determine which refresh to run. Use BEACHES from @van-beaches/shared. For tides: filter out beaches with null tideStationId, then deduplicate by stationId using a Set (same pattern as server/src/jobs/dataRefreshJob.ts). Each individual beach refresh must be wrapped in try/catch -- log errors and continue. The ctx.waitUntil() should wrap the entire refresh operation to ensure it completes before the worker is terminated.

embedded_context.constraints: ADR-001: Cron Triggers run on a standalone Worker. Free tier target: < 800 KV writes/day. Tide refresh MUST skip null tideStationId beaches. Error in one beach must not abort the entire refresh. Non-scope: Do NOT change BEACHES data.

tasks.title: Create Pages Functions middleware for CORS and error handling
tasks.objective: Create functions/_middleware.ts that handles CORS headers and error handling for all Pages Functions, replacing the Express cors and errorHandler middleware.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: All responses include Access-Control-Allow-Origin header
OPTIONS requests return 204 with correct CORS headers without calling the next handler
When the downstream handler throws, the middleware returns a JSON error response matching ApiResponse<null> shape
acceptance_criteria.test_assertion: expect(body).toEqual({ success: false, data: null, error: expect.any(String), cached: false, cachedAt: null })

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The error response status code is 404 for NOT_FOUND errors, 500 for unhandled errors

tasks.technical_notes: Pages Functions middleware uses the onRequest export and calls context.next() to invoke the downstream handler. CORS headers: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET,OPTIONS, Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type. Error handling should catch exceptions from context.next() and return Response.json() with the ApiResponse<null> error shape. Define an AppError class (or use a simple error code check) for structured errors like NOT_FOUND.

embedded_context.constraints: Non-scope: Do NOT change the ApiResponse<T> type. The error response shape must match what the Express errorHandler currently returns. CORS must allow all origins (matching current Express cors() default).
